description: Beta blockers can narrow the airways and blunt the effect of reliever inhalers in people with asthma.
management: Make sure every prescriber knows about the asthma diagnosis. Cardioselective agents are preferred when a beta blocker is essential.
source_name: FDA labelling for beta-adrenergic blocking agents (Warnings)

description: A minority of people with asthma (especially with nasal polyps) have NSAID-exacerbated respiratory disease, where aspirin or NSAIDs trigger severe wheezing.
description_note: This applies only to people with a known reaction history.
management: Report any previous wheeze after aspirin or ibuprofen to the prescriber before taking these medicines.

description: NSAIDs, aspirin and steroids can cause or worsen stomach and duodenal ulcers and bleeding.
management: Gastric protection or an alternative painkiller is usually considered. Report black stools, vomiting blood or severe stomach pain urgently.

description: NSAIDs reduce blood flow inside the kidneys and can worsen existing kidney disease.
management: Kidney function should be reviewed before and during use; alternatives are often preferred.

description: Metformin is cleared by the kidneys; reduced kidney function raises the risk of lactic acidosis.
management: Metformin dosing depends on measured kidney function (eGFR) and is set by the prescriber.
source_name: FDA label for metformin hydrochloride (Boxed Warning)

description: Reduced kidney function makes high potassium much more likely with potassium supplements or potassium-sparing diuretics.
management: Potassium blood tests are essential; dosing is prescriber-directed.

description: Active liver disease is a caution for statins, which are metabolised by the liver.
management: Liver blood tests guide the prescriber's decision.

description: The maximum safe daily dose of acetaminophen (paracetamol) is lower in liver disease, and it is present in many combination cold and pain products.
management: Check every product label for acetaminophen/paracetamol and confirm your daily limit with a pharmacist.
source_name: FDA Drug Safety Communication on acetaminophen hepatotoxicity

description: NSAIDs are generally avoided from 20 weeks of pregnancy because of effects on fetal kidneys and amniotic fluid, and after 30 weeks because of the fetal ductus arteriosus.
management: Any pain relief in pregnancy should be confirmed with the obstetric team.
source_name: FDA Drug Safety Communication: NSAIDs after 20 weeks of pregnancy

description: ACE inhibitors and ARBs can seriously harm a developing fetus and carry a boxed warning against use in pregnancy.
management: Contact the prescriber urgently if pregnancy is suspected while taking these medicines.

description: Tetracyclines can affect developing teeth and bone and are generally avoided in pregnancy.
management: An alternative antibiotic is usually chosen; confirm with the prescriber.

description: Methotrexate and warfarin are known to cause fetal harm and are contraindicated or tightly restricted in pregnancy.
management: Urgent prescriber contact is needed if pregnancy is possible.

description: NSAIDs cause fluid retention and can worsen heart failure.
management: Report new swelling, weight gain or breathlessness; alternatives are preferred.

description: Verapamil reduces heart muscle contractility and is generally avoided in reduced-ejection-fraction heart failure.
management: Prescriber decision based on the type of heart failure.

description: Corticosteroids raise blood glucose, which can destabilise diabetes control during a course.
management: More frequent glucose checks are often advised; ask about a temporary plan.

description: Fluoroquinolones can cause both low and high blood sugar, with severe hypoglycaemia reported in people on glucose-lowering medicines.
management: Monitor glucose more closely during the antibiotic course.
source_name: FDA Drug Safety Communication on fluoroquinolones

description: Tramadol lowers the seizure threshold and is a caution in people with epilepsy.
management: Alternative pain relief is usually preferred; prescriber decision.

description: Fluoroquinolones can affect the central nervous system and lower the seizure threshold.
management: Flag the epilepsy diagnosis to the prescriber.
source_name: FDA Drug Safety Communication on fluoroquinolones

description: NSAIDs raise blood pressure and reduce the effect of several antihypertensive medicines.
management: Blood pressure should be monitored if NSAIDs are used regularly.

description: Thiazide diuretics raise uric acid and can precipitate gout attacks.
management: Mention gout history so the prescriber can weigh alternatives.

description: Anticholinergic medicines can raise eye pressure in narrow-angle glaucoma.
management: Flag glaucoma to the prescriber and report eye pain or blurred vision.

description: Opioids and benzodiazepines depress breathing, which is riskier in significant COPD.
management: Only under prescriber direction; seek help for increasing breathlessness or drowsiness.
source_name: FDA Boxed Warning: opioids with benzodiazepines
